XI. Id q; Iuuenal. opinor, illud indicat: (retur: Palleat vt nudis qui pressit calcibus anguem: Aut Lugdunensem Rhetor dicturus ad aram.

XII. Augustus Cæsar, Portius Latro, Demo-sthenes, aliiq; plurimi declamitare sunt soliti: ipse Cicero, cuius merito apud omnes valere debet authoritas, nō Romæ solū, verū et Athenis, & in Asia, de-clamando sese exercuit: quodā etiā in loco fatetur, aridam atq; ieiunam orationis suæ futuram facultatem fuisse, nisi ad declamandi se exercitationes cotulisset.
XIII. Itaq; tuum institutum vehementer laudo probo: imprimis vero quod modo bono difficultatem illam superasse te intelligo, quæ ab hoc exer-citationis genere auocare plurimos consueuit.

page.notes: Scan is cropped at the left; the left half of the image is the edge of the neighbouring page, not transcribed. "(retur:" and the "Id q;" abbreviation are uncertain. The gathering mark "ñ 2" is doubtful. The "[?]" on the signature marks that reading. The verse in XI is set as one paragraph with line breaks not preserved. Spellings such as "solent", "suiq;", "sese" and "insarcire" are normalised from long s and u/v as instructed; the original form of "insarcire" is uncertain.
